brief: The canvas displays a field of connected, fluid cells. These cells, initially defined by soft, luminous boundaries, continuously replicate in a self-sustaining process. When two adjacent cells reach maturity, the constriction point between them visibly intensifies, glowing with a bright internal light and undergoing a rhythmic pulsation. This constriction visibly tightens, causing the parent cell to contract and pinch off a newly formed, distinct daughter cell. The process repeats autonomously, resulting in exponentially increasing clusters of stable, membrane-defined cells across the viewing area.

statement: This sketch depicts an autonomous system of cellular replication where individual cells grow and mature through a process of pulsating expansion. When mature, cells enter a contraction phase that visually pinches off new daughter cells, creating a continuous cycle of reproduction. The visual design distinguishes between developing and mature cells: growing cells exhibit soft boundaries with pulsating effects, while mature cells display rigid, stable membranes. The system evolves organically across the canvas, generating complex clusters of interconnected cells through self-sustained replication without external input or control.
